headline: A one-time charge masks an otherwise healthy quarter
summary_short: AECOM (fiscal Q3 2026) took a $337 million pre-tax charge on a delayed Construction Management project, swinging to a $76.0 million operating loss even as backlog rose 13% to a record $27.8 billion.
summary_long: Revenue fell 14.2% y/y to $3,586.1M and the company swung to a $76.0M operating loss, driven entirely by a $337M pre-tax charge from a higher projected cost to complete a Construction Management project awarded in 2019 under legacy risk terms. Excluding that charge, adjusted EBITDA would have risen 5% to $329M and adjusted EPS 11% to $1.49, and design-business net service revenue grew 4% y/y (6% Americas, 4% International). Backlog reached a record $27.8B (+13% y/y) on a 1.6 book-to-burn ratio. Management lowered FY2026 NSR-growth and free-cash-flow expectations to reflect the charge but held its ex-charge adjusted EPS ($5.90-$6.10) and adjusted EBITDA ($1,275-$1,305M) guidance. Net leverage was 1.5x.
confidence_notes: AECOM's fiscal year ends September 30, so this release is labeled "third quarter fiscal 2026" (fiscal Q3, Apr-Jun) by the company; the shard files it under the calendar-quarter label FY2026 Q2. Reported operating income, net income, and EPS are dominated by a one-time $337M Construction Management project charge — the release's own ex-charge adjusted figures (EBITDA, EPS) are materially stronger and are captured separately in extendedMetrics/guidance rather than blended into the primary GAAP KPI row.

drivers.explanation: Swing to an operating loss was driven by a $337M pre-tax charge for a higher projected cost to complete a Construction Management project bid in 2019 under legacy risk terms.
Follows directly from the Construction Management project charge flowing through operating income; excluding the charge, adjusted EBITDA rose 5% and adjusted EPS rose 11%.
The charge reduced reported revenue directly, while underlying design-business net service revenue still grew 4% y/y (6% Americas, 4% International).
Record $4.2 billion of wins produced a 1.6 book-to-burn ratio, including two of the largest recompetes in company history with expanded scope.
Management called the construction-charge loss disappointing but pointed to record wins, an all-time-high backlog, and strong underlying margins as evidence of business health.
